hypotheses.construction_plan: Take F(theta)=polygamma(0,theta). The first member is F evaluated at theta=z; the second member is dF/dtheta evaluated at theta=z. The raw expression is the sum of these two generated members.
required_assumptions: polygamma(0, theta) is differentiable at theta=z
the derivative of polygamma(0, theta) is polygamma(1, theta)
hypotheses.rationale: The expression contains two consecutive orders of the polygamma function; polygamma(1,z) is the first derivative of polygamma(0,z). Thus the two terms are generated from the digamma function by identity and differentiation.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Define a two-parameter template P(n,theta)=polygamma(n,theta). Specializing n=0 and theta=z gives the first term; specializing n=1 and theta=z gives the second term. The raw expression is the sum of these two specializations.
required_assumptions: polygamma(n, theta) is defined for n in {0,1} at theta=z
hypotheses.rationale: The two terms are successive members of the polygamma family indexed by the order parameter n.
